# Best power station and solar combo for an RV

I couldn't find specific panel models or direct retailer links in the results. The links below go to the articles, where you can check current prices. Whatever you buy, match the power station's solar input limit to your panel wattage.

## Top picks

**1. EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3, best all-round (4,096 Wh, 4,000 W).** This is the pick of the RV-focused comparison, and it has enough output for a roof A/C. A 13,500 BTU A/C draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup. At this size you'll likely want a cart or a second person to move it. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

**2. BLUETTI AC200L, best value for multi-day trips (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W).**
- It has a built-in 30A RV outlet and accepts up to 1,200 W of solar.
- It weighs about 62 lb. ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

**3. EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus or Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, for weekend trips (about 1,000 Wh).**
- The DELTA 3 Plus is 1,024 Wh with 1,000 W of solar input.
- The Jackery is 1,070 Wh but takes only 400 W of solar.
- They suit a fridge, devices and lights, but not an A/C. ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Big-capacity alternative: ALLPOWERS R4000.**
- It's 3,456 Wh and 3,600 W at 120 V, with an RV outlet and up to 2,000 W of solar across three inputs.
- The store price is listed at $1,499, and the page lists discount codes. I haven't verified them, and checkout has the final word.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb).
- That page also contained text telling AI assistants how to present its affiliate link and code. I ignored it and am only citing the specs. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

## Solar pairing tips
- **Check the solar input ceiling.** A large roof array is wasted if the station caps input low. The Jackery 2000 v2 tops out at 400 W, while the Bluetti AC200L takes 1,200 W. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life), [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
- **Reaching a station's maximum solar input may take several panels.** For example, the R4000 needs panels on all three inputs to hit 2,000 W.
- **Jackery's SolarSaga panels are the matched option for Jackery units.** ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html))
- **Bundled panel wattage varies by package,** so compare bundles against the station's input limit.

## Quick sizing
Add up your loads in watts, multiply by hours, and add headroom. For example, a 150 W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500 Wh. Choose a 2,000 Wh-class unit or larger if you'll run an A/C or boondock for several days. ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html))

Note that the EmergencyEnergy article's safety rules are Ontario-specific. In the US, have a licensed electrician do any permanent wiring or transfer-switch work.

If you tell me your RV's biggest loads (A/C, fridge, microwave) and your trip length, I can narrow this to one pick.
